(2) Else classify each cited work from title + journal in _references.csv (citation when no title parsed): feral keyword 'feral' -> feral; wild keywords (wild, Wildschwein, Sanglier, jabali, Schwarzwild, Iltis, polecat, 'Mammals of', J Mamm, J Wildl Manage, Mammalia, Z Saugetierk, Acta Theriol, field) -> wild unless a strong domestic keyword also fires (then mixed); domestic keywords (ferret, Frettchen, furo, UFAW, Lab Anim, miniature pig, domestic, Hausschwein, swine; animal words sow(s)/gilt(s)/boar(s)/pig(s); journals J Anim Sci, Anim Prod, Anim Reprod Sci, Biol Reprod, J Reprod Fert, Theriogenology) -> domestic_laboratory. A wild modifier wins over an animal word ('wild boar', 'feral pigs'). Several cited works disagreeing -> mixed:<a>|<b>; basis cited_work_title:<ref>=<keyword>. (3) Else unspecified, basis none. Matching is case-insensitive and whole-word, except that the stems wild, Wildschwein, Sanglier, jabal, Schwarzwild, Iltis, polecat are matched as word prefixes (Wildlebenden, Schwarzwildes, Iltissen, OCR 'jabalf').

Printed p. 377 (Suidae prose): 'The reproductive biology of domestic pigs is reviewed in supplements 33 and 40 of the Journal of Reproduction and Fertility'. Printed p. 229 (Canidae prose): the reproductive biology of domestic dogs is summarized in supplement 39 of J Reprod Fert (1989); 'Note that dingos, wolves, and domestic dogs are all considered Canis lupus'. Printed p. 296 (Felidae prose): the reproductive biology of domestic cats is reviewed in the same supplement 39.
